endpoints.name: endUsers.create
endpoints.description: Creates an end user: one of your customers, mapped to one QuickBooks Desktop company file. Next, create an auth session so the end user can connect QuickBooks. `sourceId` must be unique within the project.

pathParams.name: id

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the end user.

endpoints.name: endUsers.delete
endpoints.description: Permanently deletes the end user, its connection, its Web Connector credentials and its stored request data. The Web Connector on the end user's computer stops working for this application; remove the application from the Web Connector afterwards.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the end user.

endpoints.name: endUsers.resetCompanyFile
endpoints.description: Re-binds the connection after the company file was moved or renamed (`mode: path`) or the company itself was renamed (`mode: identity`), which otherwise leaves the connection in `company_file_mismatch` or `QBD_COMPANY_FILE_NOT_FOUND`. Ask the end user to open the correct company file in QuickBooks first. The connection checks the file at the next Web Connector check-in. Queued requests stay queued.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the end user.

endpoints.name: authSessions.create
endpoints.description: Creates a time-limited link to the hosted setup flow, where the end user connects their QuickBooks Desktop company file through the QuickBooks Web Connector. Create a new auth session each time you show the link; each one expires after `linkExpiryMins`.

endpoints.name: endUsers.passthrough
endpoints.description: Sends qbXML request elements directly to the end user's QuickBooks Desktop and returns QuickBooks' response. Send JSON (`application/json`) or a `<QBXMLMsgsRq>` fragment (`application/xml`); the response uses the same format. We add the qbXML envelope, `onError="stopOnError"` unless you set it, and a `newMessageSetID` for writes. A body that contains any element other than a query (`...QueryRq`) is a write: send an `Idempotency-Key` to make retries safe. A read-only secret key can send only queries; a write returns `403 API_KEY_READ_ONLY`. The response is `200` with each message's own status; the call fails only when QuickBooks processed no message successfully. Each call creates a request resource (`Daapi-Request-Id`).

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the end user.

pathParams.name: integrationSlug
pathParams.description: Always `quickbooks_desktop`.

endpoints.name: qbd.healthCheck
endpoints.description: Runs a real round trip to the end user's QuickBooks Desktop: the request waits for the Web Connector, opens the company file and reads company information. Use it before a sync, or to show connection status to the end user. On failure the error explains the cause and fix (for example `INTEGRATION_CONNECTION_NOT_ACTIVE` or `QBD_MODAL_DIALOG_OPEN`). The default wait is 60 seconds. Health checks keep working when billing pauses production data requests.

endpoints.name: requests.list
endpoints.description: Returns the project's QuickBooks-bound requests, newest first, from the request log (kept 30 days). Filter by end user, status, operation and creation time. The log is updated within seconds of each status change; retrieve a request for its timeline, diagnosis and result. Calls rejected before they were queued are listed as `failed` with their `errorCode` when they named an end user of this project that has a connection; rate-limited calls and calls without a resolvable end user are not.

queryParams.name: cursor
queryParams.description: The `nextCursor` from the previous page.

queryParams.name: limit
queryParams.description: Page size, 1–100. Default 50.

queryParams.name: endUserId
queryParams.description: Only requests for this end user.

queryParams.name: status
queryParams.description: Only requests in these statuses. Repeat the parameter for several (`?status=failed&status=outcome_unknown`).

items.description: `queued`: accepted and waiting for its turn or the next Web Connector check-in. `waiting_for_connection`: async request waiting for an offline connection. `sent`: handed to QuickBooks; it can no longer be canceled. `succeeded` and `failed` are final. `canceled`: canceled before it was sent. `outcome_unknown`: a write was sent and its result could not be confirmed.

queryParams.name: operationId
queryParams.description: Only requests for this operation, for example `qbd.invoices.create`.

queryParams.name: createdAfter
queryParams.description: Only requests created at or after this time (ISO 8601).

queryParams.name: createdBefore
queryParams.description: Only requests created before this time (ISO 8601).

endpoints.name: requests.retrieve
endpoints.description: Returns a QuickBooks-bound request with its status, queue position, timeline, diagnosis, native status and result. With `waitSeconds`, the call waits up to that long for the request to finish (or become `outcome_unknown`) before answering. Use it after `504 QBD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` or a `202` async response to collect the result without resending. A call that was rejected before it was queued (for example `INTEGRATION_CONNECTION_NOT_SET_UP`, a validation error or a disabled connection) is retrievable under the request ID its error returned, as a `failed` request with `sentAt: null`, the catalog `error` for its code and no result, when it named an end user of this project that has a connection.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the request.

queryParams.name: waitSeconds
queryParams.description: Seconds to wait for a final status, 0–60. Default 0.

endpoints.name: requests.cancel
endpoints.description: Cancels a request that has not been sent to QuickBooks (`queued` or `waiting_for_connection`). Nothing reaches QuickBooks; the request becomes `canceled` with `REQUEST_CANCELED`, and a waiting synchronous call returns that error. A request that was already sent cannot be canceled (`409 REQUEST_NOT_CANCELABLE`). Canceling a canceled request returns it unchanged.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the request.

endpoints.name: webhookEndpoints.create
endpoints.description: Registers an HTTPS endpoint for events of this project. The response contains the signing secret once. Deliveries are signed with the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) scheme (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`), retried on failure for about 27 hours (after 5 s, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 5 h, 10 h and 10 h) and recorded in the delivery log. A project can have up to 20 endpoints.

endpoints.description: Returns a webhook endpoint. The signing secret is not included; rotate it to get a new one.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the webhook endpoint.

endpoints.name: webhookEndpoints.update
endpoints.description: Updates the URL, event types, description, `enabled` or `includeSyncRequests`. Omitted fields are unchanged. Re-enabling an endpoint that was disabled after failed deliveries clears `disabledReason`.

pathParams.name: id

endpoints.name: webhookEndpoints.delete
endpoints.description: Deletes the endpoint and its delivery log. Pending retries stop.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the webhook endpoint.

endpoints.name: webhookEndpoints.rotateSecret
endpoints.description: Creates a new signing secret and returns it once. For 24 hours deliveries carry two signatures (new and previous secret, space separated in `webhook-signature`), so you can deploy the new secret without dropping events.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the webhook endpoint.

endpoints.name: webhookEndpoints.sendTestEvent
endpoints.description: Sends a signed `webhook.test` event to the endpoint now (one attempt, no retries) and returns the delivery with the attempt result. Use it to check your signature verification. The endpoint receives it even when disabled.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Unique identifier for the webhook endpoint.

pathParams.description: QuickBooks ID of the sales order.

endpoints.name: qbd.salesOrders.update
endpoints.description: Changes the fields you send on an existing sales order and leaves omitted fields unchanged. Requires the current `revisionNumber`. A stale `revisionNumber` returns `409 QBD_REVISION_NUMBER_STALE`: retrieve the sales order, reapply your change and send the new revision. Sending a line array replaces all existing lines of that kind. Line arrays you omit stay unchanged: when you send only some of them, the API first reads the transaction (a separate read in the request log) and keeps the omitted lines by ID, because QuickBooks would otherwise delete them. See [Updates and line items](https://www.desktopaccountingapi.com/docs/quickbooks/updates-and-line-items/).

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: QuickBooks ID of the sales order.

pathParams.name: id

items.description: `request.succeeded`, `request.failed`, `request.canceled`: a request reached that status. `request.outcome_unknown`: a write was sent without a confirmed result. `request.outcome_resolved`: such a write was resolved. `connection.setup_completed`: an end user finished setup and the first check passed. `connection.status_changed`: the derived connection status changed (offline is announced after it holds for 30 seconds).

eventTypes.description: Event types to deliver. At least one.

description.description: Your note about the endpoint, up to 500 characters.

includeSyncRequests.description: Also deliver request events for synchronous calls whose caller already received the result. Default `false`: synchronous requests produce events only when the caller did not get the final result (timeout after sending, disconnect) or the outcome is unknown.
